question: Roots of which of the following plants can give rise to new plants?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sweet Potato**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The roots of the **Sweet Potato** have the ability to give rise to new plants. This process occurs through a phenomenon known as **vegetative propagation**.
 
• **Sweet Potato roots** are modified adventitious roots that store food and can develop shoots, which eventually grow into a new plant under suitable conditions.
 
• Unlike other plants like **Maize, Potato, and Gram**, which propagate through seeds, tubers, or other parts, the vegetative propagation of sweet potatoes is specifically through roots.
 
• In vegetative propagation, a part of the plant other than seeds is used to grow new plants. This is commonly seen in crops like **Sweet Potato, Dahlia, and Turmeric**.
 
• This method is widely used in agriculture and gardening as it ensures the propagation of plants with identical genetic properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sweet Potato:**

 
 
• It is a dicotyledonous plant belonging to the family **Convolvulaceae**.
 
• Sweet potatoes are rich in **carbohydrates, vitamins (especially Vitamin A), and dietary fiber**, making them an important food crop.
 
• They are primarily grown in tropical and subtropical regions, with **India, China, and the United States** being major producers.
 
• They are propagated through vegetative means such as **root slips or cuttings**.
 
 
 
• **Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• This is a form of asexual reproduction where new plants are produced from the **roots, stems, or leaves** of the parent plant.
 
• Examples include **Sweet Potato (roots), Potato (stem tubers), Ginger (rhizomes), and Bryophyllum (leaves)**.
 
• This method is advantageous as it is faster, bypasses the seed stage, and retains the parental plant's genetic characteristics.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Options:**
 
 
• **Maize:** Propagates through seeds and cannot regenerate from roots.
 
• **Potato:** Propagates through **stem tubers**, not roots.
 
• **Gram:** Propagates through seeds only.
 
• **Sweet Potato:** Propagates through roots, which can generate new plants, making it the correct answer.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Importance:**
 
 
• Vegetative propagation ensures uniform crop quality, which is vital in commercial farming.
 
• It also allows propagation of plants that produce few or no viable seeds, such as **Sweet Potato**.
 
• Additionally, it enables cultivation in regions where seed germination is difficult due to climatic conditions.
